task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) full from-scratch re-check of REQ-157's design after rework commit 290c6b2, which claimed to fix section 4.3's `now`-stub closure and section 4.1's 8-row matrix-table closures. Explicitly instructed not to trust prior partial re-skims (two prior rounds each missed a violation the other had introduced/overlooked).

checks_performed.full_document_read: Read all 619 lines of lib/letflow/design/req157-lua-capability-model.md top to bottom, independently of step-01-code-designer.json's self-report.
checks_performed.code_fragment_grep: Grepped for `fn `, `raise `, `case `, `cond `, `do:`, `->`, `Lua.set!(lua, [:platform` throughout the full document. Findings: (1) lines 255-256 `@type required_capability_fun :: (args :: [term()] -> ...)` and `@type stub_fun :: (args :: [term()] -> [term()])` -- permitted @type arrow-signatures, not code bodies. (2) Every `Lua.set!(lua, [:platform, ...` occurrence (lines 283, 535, 550, 595) is a prose description of a call pattern (partial expression referenced by name, no full literal statement with a body/closure argument) -- none is a complete copy-paste-ready expression. (3) The section-0 citation of `lua_script_audit.ex`'s EXISTING (already-shipped, pre-REQ-157) rescue clause (`rescue e in [Lua.RuntimeException, Lua.CompilerException] -> {:error, Exception.message(e)}`) is a verbatim quote of code that already exists in the repository today, cited for compatibility context (this design must not require an edit to it) -- not implementation code this design is proposing; consistent treatment across all three review rounds, never flagged. (4) Section 4.3's former `fn _args -> [Platform.now()] end` closure is gone, replaced by prose (line ~336-339: 'the now row's stub ignores its argument list and returns Platform.now/0's result wrapped as the single-element Lua return list...'). (5) Section 4.1's matrix table (lines 269-278) now contains only prose behavior descriptions in the 'required' column ('Ignores all but the first argument... and returns Capabilities.service_capability(svc_id)', 'Ignores its arguments and always returns the constant string...', etc.) -- no `fn` literals remain in any of the 8 rows. No other code-shaped fragment found anywhere in the document outside the two permitted @type lines.
checks_performed.sections_4_4_and_6_1_regression: Re-confirmed clean (unchanged from iteration-1 fix, still prose-only): 4.4's install/2 fold is a 4-step numbered prose description explicitly labelled 'a description of required behavior, not an Elixir expression'; 6.1's raise shape is a 5-row table of keyword-list keys, explicitly labelled 'a description of the required shape, not an Elixir expression.'
checks_performed.acceptance_criteria_mapping: Read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-157 entry directly (owner ELIXIR-DEV, status pending, depends_on [REQ-153]) and confirmed all 8 acceptance_criteria strings verbatim-match section 7's traceability table rows 1-8, each mapped to a concrete design element (capability matrix, check!/3, denial shape, call_service parameterisation, now/fail :none short-circuit, moduledoc requirement, mix test/compile note).
checks_performed.substance_regression_check: Capability matrix content (4.1), denial shape (2.3), call_service parameterisation (4.2), now/fail ungated rationale (5), cross-module dependency table (8), test suite spec (9), invariants INV-CAP-1..4 (10), and open questions OQ-1..3 (11) all present, internally consistent, and unchanged in substance from the prior PASS-on-substance version.
checks_performed.git_verification: `git log --oneline -8` confirms the claimed history (19abb6a original design, d3938a3/b88e051 iteration-1 fail cycle, 3680243/6e0f441 rework 1, 290c6b2/f9b3a0b rework 2). `git show 290c6b2 --stat` confirms only step-01-code-designer.json and lib/letflow/design/req157-lua-capability-model.md changed (27 lines in the design doc, 17 insertions/16 deletions), consistent with the claimed section 4.1 + 4.3 scope.

result.verdict_statement: PASS. No implementation code (no real .ex/.exs bodies) remains anywhere in the design document -- all four previously-found violations (4.4's fold body, 6.1's raise expression, 4.3's now-stub closure, 4.1's 8-row matrix closures) are fixed and no fifth was found on this full independent re-read. All 8 acceptance criteria are mapped to concrete, unambiguous design elements. The design is ready for WF-02 Step 2 (ELIXIR-DEV implementation).
